$comment: Trackside cameras (packages/trackside/README.md): how car numbers are read and grouped into trainsets. guess unless noted; OPEN-QUESTIONS #32.

cars.$pattern: Car numbers as painted: three digits on Mk I, Mk II and Mk III cars, four on Mk V (test videos 2026-10-01 and 2026-10-03 near Main Street–Science World and Stadium–Chinatown, Braden).
cars.$minConfidence: Readings below this mean digit probability (0–1) aren't reported as cars (only as uncertain crops). In the test videos every correct reading scored 0.9–1.00 and every wrong one 0.6–0.75 (Mk I numbers, too small at that zoom). guess
cars.$maxHeightFraction: Text boxes taller than this fraction of the image are windows or livery, not numbers. guess

fleets.$comment: Which fleet a car number belongs to (Expo and Millennium Lines), and how its cars are grouped. A set of `setSize` consecutively numbered cars, the first numbered 1 more than a multiple of `setSize`, always runs together: Mk I and Mk II married pairs (035·036, 097·098, 101·102, 309·310, 319·320, 331·332, 335·336), Mk III 4-car sets (421–424, 441–444, 473–476, 477–480), all seen in the test videos. The number ranges are guesses from those sightings. Mk V cars run in 5-car articulated sets whose numbering doesn't follow that rule (6025 6024 6023 6022 6011 and 6225 6224 6223 6222 6211, read in that order), so they have no setSize.
